messages.content: what are the tools u know for booking flights

function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common “tools” (websites, apps, APIs, and platforms) you can use to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers |
|----------|----------------|----------------|
| **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | One‑stop shop for flights, hotels, car rentals, and vacation packages. |
| | **Kayak** | Aggregates prices from many airlines and OTAs; offers price alerts and flexible‑date searches. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global flight search engine; great for comparing fares across airlines and dates. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast, intuitive interface; shows price trends, alternative airports, and multi‑city itineraries. |
| | **Momondo** | Similar to Skyscanner but often finds slightly cheaper fares; includes “price calendar” view. |
| | **Priceline** | Known for “Name Your Own Price” and “Express Deals” for last‑minute bookings. |
| | **Orbitz** | Offers loyalty points (Orbucks) and bundle discounts. |
| | **Travelocity** | Similar to Orbitz; often runs promotions for bundled travel. |
| | **Hotwire** | Focuses on discounted “opaque” fares; good for budget travelers. |
| | **CheapOair** | Specializes in low‑fare tickets and offers a mobile app. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Great for spontaneous trips; bundles flights, hotels, and activities. |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia; offers competitive fares and local support. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA with a focus on package deals. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels, but also offers flight bookings in some regions. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts you to flash sales and price drops. |
| | **Hopper** | Uses predictive analytics to tell you when to book. |
| | **Travelzoo** | Curated deals and coupons for flights and travel. |
| | **Trafalgar** | Luxury travel agency; offers curated itineraries. |
| | **JetRadar** | Aggregates flight data from multiple sources; good for price comparison. |
| | **FlightNetwork** | Aggregates fares from many airlines; offers “price alerts.” |
| | **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network that aggregates flight data; useful for developers. |
| | **Travelport** | Global distribution system (GDS) used by travel agencies; offers API access. |
| | **Amadeus** | Another GDS; provides APIs for flight search, booking, and ancillary services. |
| | **Sabre** | Classic GDS; offers APIs for flight inventory, pricing, and booking. |
| | **TravelSky** | Chinese GDS; used by many Chinese carriers and agencies. |
| | **ITA Software** | Provides flight search and pricing engines; used by many OTAs. |
| | **OpenSky API** | Real‑time flight data; not for booking but useful for flight tracking. |
| | **FlightAware API** | Flight status and tracking; can be integrated into booking workflows. |
| | **FlightStats API** | Provides flight schedules, delays, and historical data. |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Allows developers to embed flight search into their own sites/apps. |
| | **Google Flights API** | (Limited public access) – can be used for flight search and price alerts. |
| | **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** | Includes flight search, booking, and ancillary services. |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Offers flight search, booking, and ancillary services. |
| | **Travelport APIs** | Provides flight search, booking, and ancillary services. |
| | **Airline APIs** | Many airlines (e.g., Delta, United, Lufthansa) offer direct APIs for flight search and booking. |
| | **Travel Agency Software** | e.g., **Sabre Red Workspace**, **Amadeus Altea**, **Travelport Galileo** – used by professional travel agents. |
| | **Mobile Apps** | Most OTAs have dedicated iOS/Android apps (Expedia, Kayak, Skyscanner, Google Flights, Hopper). |
| | **Voice Assistants** | Alexa, Google Assistant, Siri can book flights via integrated skills or shortcuts. |
| | **Chatbots** | Many airlines and OTAs have chatbots on their websites or messaging platforms (WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger). |
| | **Travel Aggregator APIs** | e.g., **Travelpayouts**, **Skyscanner**, **Google Flights** – for embedding flight search into custom apps. |
| | **Price Alert Services** | e.g., **Hopper**, **Google Flights**, **Skyscanner**, **Airfarewatchdog** – notify you when fares drop. |
| | **Travel Loyalty Programs** | e.g., **Miles & More**, **SkyMiles**, **AAdvantage** – can be used to redeem miles for flights. |
| | **Corporate Travel Platforms** | e.g., **Concur**, **Egencia**, **SAP Ariba Travel** – for business travel booking. |
| | **Travel Management Companies (TMCs)** | e.g., **CWT**, **Boeing Business Travel**, **American Express Global Business Travel** – provide corporate booking solutions. |
| | **Travel Aggregator Websites** | e.g., **Google Flights**, **Skyscanner**, **Kayak** – aggregate data from airlines and OTAs. |
| | **Travel Aggregator Mobile Apps** | e.g., **Hopper**, **Skyscanner**, **Google Flights** – for on‑the‑go booking. |
| | **Travel Aggregator APIs** | e.g., **Skyscanner**, **Google Flights**, **Travelpayouts** – for developers. |
| | **Travel Aggregator Platforms** | e.g., **Travelport**, **Amadeus**, **Sabre** – used by agencies and OTAs. |
